# Reference workload

Run `npm run --silent workload > workload-report.json` from the generated loan application after installing its locked dependencies. It builds the production UI, then starts the actual production API entry on a private loopback port. It does not use the developer database or `.env.local`. The command writes one JSON report to stdout and build/child diagnostics to stderr. Exit 1 means a measured target or coverage requirement failed; inspect `reasons`. Interruptions clean up owned processes and the temporary database. No database path or duration override is accepted.

Each run seeds a new database with 2,000 synthetic users, 10,000 items and 50,000 loans, including 5,000 active loans evenly owned by the 20 baseline clients. All passwords and signing material are generated per run; one real password hash is reused for synthetic identities. It uses real CSRF/session sign-in. Twenty clients cycle list/reserve/return at 70/20/10 with 250 ms think time. The reference window has 30 seconds of warm-up followed by 120 measured seconds, five simultaneous attempts on one item every 10 seconds, four distinct-account sign-ins after each burst, and a separate SQLite writer held for two seconds halfway through measurement. Authentication probes and bursts share the same 20-request concurrency bound and are reported separately from operation latency samples.

The report records successful DTO-validated and all-attempt p50/p95/p99 separately, response statuses and unexpected errors, server peak RSS sampled every 10 ms, event-loop delay, burst outcomes, sign-in coverage and independent post-run duplicate-active-loan/FK checks. A busy refusal is expected only while its request overlaps the observed external writer. Refusals cannot supply successful latency samples. Passing the measured targets requires at least 5,000 successful operation samples, every operation p95 at most 200 ms, zero unexpected errors, peak RSS at most 300,000,000 bytes, observed event-loop p95 at most 200 ms, twelve one-winner/four-conflict bursts, all sign-in probes and observed bounded busy degradation.

`npm run workload:smoke` runs a two-second diagnostic, including the full dataset and real owned child processes. Its successful exit means the diagnostic completed; `referencePass` is always false. It is suitable for functional regression checks, never for performance qualification.

Run the full workload alone on the specified reference machine. The report records OS, architecture, Node and total memory, but cannot verify reference-hardware identity or isolation. Every report remains `qualification: unqualified`. The existing application rate/security controls are unchanged: rate refusals, inadequate coverage and memory failures remain failures. There is no kernel workload receipt, baseline/trend comparison, threshold attention or accepted qualification evidence yet. Do not change limits or omit failures to manufacture a pass.
